## Goals for this talk

- Provide background information on AI for Bioinformatics.
- Cover the NIH Responsible AI Policy.
- Equip you with practical tips for minimizing the risks of using LLMs & agents for bioinformatics.

:::{.column width="15%"}
:::

:::{.callout-tip .column width="70%" .xx-large-text .fragment}
### Take-home message

By the end, you should feel empowered with the knowledge to
**use agentic LLMs proficiently** for bioinformatics,
without compromising the **quality of your science**.

:::

## NIH AI Use Checklist

::::: {.columns .x-large-text}

:::: {.column width="47%" }

:::{.callout-warning .fragment}
### Stop and Reconsider If:
- You cannot verify the output
- You cannot explain or justify the result
- The task involves high-stakes decisions without expert review
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .fragment}
### 1. Confirm the Use is Appropriate
- Can you clearly state what you need, your audience (e.g., internal, external), and why AI helps?
- Do you have the time and expertise to review and adapt the output?
- Are you using a federally approved or authorized tool?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .fragment}
### 2. Define the Human-AI Roles
- What task is the AI performing (e.g., drafting, summarizing, classifying)?
- What decisions will you make (vs. the AI)?
- Are you prepared to be accountable for how outputs are used?
:::

::::

::::{.column width="3%"}
::::

:::: {.column width="47%"}

:::{.callout-note icon=false .fragment}
### 3. Project Data and Outputs
- Does your input data include clinical, sensitive, identifiable, or restricted information?
- Is that data allowed in the tool you are using (e.g., consistent with consent, IRB decision, agreements)?
- Are you sharing only the minimum data necessary?
- Do the outputs create new sensitivity, intellectual property, or reuse risks?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .fragment}
### 4. Verify Outputs
- Have you checked the facts, numbers, and citations?
- Have you tested outputs for errors, bias, or omissions?
- Would you be comfortable defending this output if questioned?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .fragment}
### 5. Be Transparent About AI Use
- Will others know AI was used?
- Have you documented how outputs were generated (e.g., prompts used)?
- Have you avoided presenting AI output as authoritative without review?
:::

::::

:::::

::: footer
Content retrieved September 2026 from the
[NIH AI Use Checklist](https://nih.sharepoint.com/sites/NIH-ai/SitePages/NIH-AI-Use-Checklist.aspx).
Please refer to the official site for the latest guidance.

## Bioinformaticians design, develop, and execute code {.x-large-text}

:::{.callout-note icon=false .column width="30%" .xx-large-text .fragment}
### Design

:::: {.align-center}
{{< fa brain size=2x >}} &nbsp; {{< fa palette size=2x >}}
:::

- Read scientific papers, software documentation, and forums.
- Plan how to analyze data to answer a scientific question.
- Decide how new code will accomplish the analysis plan.
:::

:::{.column width="5%"}
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .column width="30%" .xx-large-text .fragment}
### Develop

:::: {.align-center}
{{< fa pen-to-square size=2x >}} &nbsp; {{< fa file-code size=2x >}}
::::

- Write new scripts, packages, and command line tools to accomplish the analysis plan.
- Write tests to validate the code performs as expected.
- Document how the code works and how it is used to produce results.
:::

:::{.column width="5%"}
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false .column width="30%" .xx-large-text .fragment}
### Execute

:::: {.align-center}
{{< fa person-hiking size=2x >}} &nbsp; {{< fa terminal size=2x >}}
::::

- Obtain the data from the study/experiment.
- Install necessary software dependencies.
- Run the code on the data and evaluate the results.
:::

::: {.fragment .align-center}

&nbsp;

#### _How can agents assist us in bioinformatics tasks?_

Treat agents like just another tool in your toolbox.
:::

## Reproducible practices for responsible AI use {{< fa arrows-spin >}}

::: {.column}
#### Organize your projects

- One project per directory.
- Keep data, code, and outputs in separate subdirectories.
- Data is read-only; outputs should only be written by the code.

:::

::: {.column}

```{.default filename="file system tree" code-line-numbers=false}
/data/$USER/projects
├── my-rnaseq-project
│   ├── AGENTS.md
│   ├── data/
│   ├── docs/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── results/
│   ├── scripts/
│   └── tests/
└── r-dataviz-explorer
    ├── references/
    ├── scripts/
    ├── SKILL.md
    └── tests/
```

:::

::: footer
Credit to Samarth Mathur for these project examples.
:::

## Reproducible practices for responsible AI use {{< fa arrows-spin >}}

::: {.column}
#### Organize your projects

- One project per directory.
- Keep data, code, and outputs in separate subdirectories.
- Data is read-only; outputs should only be written by the code.

#### Version control & backup with git & GitHub

- Create a git repository for each project and upload it to GitHub.
- Commit meaningful code changes and sync with GitHub frequently.

## Review, test, and validate {{< fa vial-circle-check >}}

From the NIH Responsible AI policy:

> Do not rely on the technology to be a software developer by proxy:
>
> - All well-written code must adhere to security design and ethical principles.
> - All code output needs to be reviewed for completeness, quality, efficiency, and, most of all, security.
> - Leverage manual and automated validation tools and testing technologies to help ensure these factors.
> - If you cannot identify or understand what a piece of AI generated code does, you should not use it.

_AI outputs may be incomplete, inaccurate, biased, or fabricated._

::: footer
Content retrieved September 2026 from the
[NIH Responsible AI site](https://nih.sharepoint.com/sites/NIH-ai/SitePages/Responsible-AI.aspx).
Please refer to the official site for the latest guidance.
:::

## Review {{< fa vial-circle-check >}}

- Read the entire output of each prompt and ensure you understand it.
- Be skeptical. Do not blindly trust that the output is complete or correct.
- Treat agents as untrustworthy, in terms of both inputs and outputs.
  - Do not expose passwords, access tokens, or sensitive information.
  - Refer to the [NIH Responsible AI page - approved tools and data types](https://nih.sharepoint.com/sites/NIH-ai/SitePages/Responsible-AI.aspx#approved-tools-and-data-types) for which types of data can be used with the tools we have access to.

::: footer
Please refer to the official [NIH Responsible AI site](https://nih.sharepoint.com/sites/NIH-ai/SitePages/Responsible-AI.aspx#approved-tools-and-data-types) for the latest guidance.
:::

## Review {{< fa vial-circle-check >}}

:::{.column}
> If you cannot identify or understand what a piece of AI generated code does, you should not use it.

:::: {.small-text}
Content retrieved September 2026 from the [NIH Responsible AI site](https://nih.sharepoint.com/sites/NIH-ai/SitePages/Responsible-AI.aspx). Please refer to the official site for the latest guidance.
::::

:::

:::{.column .fragment .callout-tip title="Challenge yourself!" .xx-large-text}
If you do not understand a piece of AI-generated code, dig into the documentation and tutorials to **learn how it works**.
:::

::::{.x-large-text}
:::{.fragment}
- Come across a **package or function** you've never seen? Find the documentation and learn how it works!
  - R: use `?` and `help()`. Python: use `help()`
  - Docs websites: <https://rdrr.io/>, <https://docspython.org/3/>
:::

:::{.fragment}
- Come across a **large chunk of code** with many patterns you don't understand?
  - Prompt the agent to explain it line-by-line. Verify the explanation by asking for sources and reading them.
:::

:::{.fragment}
- Use forums for in-depth help from people.
  - StackOverflow, biostars, Posit forum, GitHub discussions, your colleagues.
:::
::::

## Testing & validation {{< fa vial-circle-check >}}

Write tests to make sure the code behaves as expected.

- Unit tests for individual functions on trivial inputs/data.
- Integration tests run multiple functions or even an entire analysis on small & simulated datasets.
- R: `testthat`. Python: `pytest`, `unittest`

:::{.column width="35%"}
```{.default filename="file system tree" code-line-numbers=false}
my-python-project
├── data/
├── src/mypackage
│   └── main.py
└── tests
    └── test_main.py
```
:::

:::{.column width="5%"}
:::

:::{.column width="58%" .xx-large-text .fragment}
```{.python filename="src/mypackage/main.py"}
def gc_content(seq):
    """Fraction of G/C bases in a DNA sequence."""
    seq = seq.upper()
    return (seq.count("G") + seq.count("C")) / len(seq)
```

```{.python filename="tests/test_main.py"}
from mypackage.main import gc_content

def test_gc_content():
    assert gc_content("GGCC") == 1.0
    assert gc_content("ATAT") == 0.0
    assert gc_content("atgc") == 0.5
```
:::

## Testing & validation {{< fa vial-circle-check >}}

:::{.column width="47%"}
Use linters and code quality checks.

- Ensure code is formatted for readability, quality, and syntax is correct.
- Security and vulnerability scanning with GitHub Advanced Security.
- R: `air`. Python: `ruff`.
:::

:::{.column width="3%"}
:::

:::{.column width="49%" .fragment}
Use `pre-commit` to run checks automatically on every change.

![](./img/pre-commit-lint.png){width="100%"}
:::

#'
#' @param x A number
#' @param y A number
#' @returns The sum of `x` and `y`
#' @examples
#' add(1, 1)
#' add(10, 1)

  x + y
}

## Document how you are using agents {{< fa file-lines >}} {.x-large-text}

_from the very beginning of the project:_

::: {.column width="48%"}

Create a document outlining how you will and will _not_ use LLMs and agents.

```{.default filename="docs/ai-usage.md" code-line-numbers=false .medium-text}
- Human responsibilities: Formulate the problem
  statement, design the software,
  validate the results, write the interpretation.
- Agent roles: assist in generating code,
  unit tests, and function documentation.
```

:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%" .fragment}

Disclose use of LLMs and agents in commit messages, issue comments, and pull requests.

![](./img/pr-ai-usage.png)

:::

## Responsible agent use to minimize risks {.x-large-text}

&nbsp;

|  | Practice | Risks minimized   |
|--|----------|-------------------|
| {{< fa arrows-spin >}} | Follow reproducible practices       | unreproducible work, destructive agent actions |
| {{< fa vial-circle-check >}} | Review, test, and validate all code | incorrect methods, bugs, inefficiencies, malware |
| {{< fa file-lines >}} | Document everything                 | unreadable code, unusable code, lack of transparency |

## A checklist for agent-assisted Bioinformatics

::::{.column width="47%"}
:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### Check off every item in this checklist before you trust LLM-generated code
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### 1. Understand
- [ ] Can I explain what the code is doing?
- [ ] Did I review all functions, parameters, and methods?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### 2. Test
- [ ] Did I run it on a small or known dataset?
- [ ] Did I test edge cases and check expected outputs?
- [ ] Have I set up an automated testing framework (pytest, testthat, GitHub Actions)?
:::
::::

::::{.column width="3%"}
::::

::::{.column width="47%"}
:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### 3. Sanity check
- [ ] Do the results make biological sense?
- [ ] Did I check for silent problems: missing samples/genes, genome build, coordinates, strandedness, IDs?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### 4. Make it reproducible
- [ ] Are code, parameters, software versions/environment, and inputs captured?
- [ ] Is the validated code committed & synced with GitHub?
:::

:::{.callout-note icon=false}
### 5. Own it
- [ ] Am I comfortable putting my name on this analysis?
- [ ] Have I documented AI use where appropriate?
:::
::::

::: footer
Checklist credit: Vishal Koparde
:::

## Final reminders

:::{.column width="12%"}
:::

::::{.column width="67%"}
:::{.callout-warning icon=false}
### LLMs produce outputs that _look like_ a plausible response to a prompt 🦜

- View these models as another tool in your toolbox alongside IDEs, HPCs, and other software.
- Interpreting the meaning of the generated outputs is your responsibility. Treat it as a learning experience!
:::
:::{.callout-warning icon=false}
### Agentic tools can accelerate bioinformatics 🚀

- Just make sure you're facing the direction you want to go!
:::
